functional.summary: Live check against this worktree's own servers (backend process cwd verified as this checkout). The whole feature now works end to end. All 106 statement rows carry an Actual control - up from 25 in task 2, because leaves are now activatable - and the prototype's 'Click any Actual to see its transactions' copy is present now that it is true. Drilling the leaf 'Petrol and Diesel Charges' (GL 55010901) returns four transaction lines in seven columns - Month, Posting date, Debit, Credit, Value, Reference, Memo - sorted Value descending, and the footer totals 22,500.00 exactly matching that leaf's Actual cell on the statement, with the prototype's 'Matches the Actual in the report' note beside it. Decision 0024 holds live: opening an aggregate issued ZERO network calls, measured by wrapping window.fetch. Drilling a leaf from inside the aggregate panel swaps the body in place - one dialog in the DOM, not two - and the breadcrumb's 'Admin Expenses' Back control returns to the 38-row group list with focus on the leaf row's Actual that was used.
manual_validation_steps: Confirmed the backend process cwd resolves to this worktree before trusting anything; frontend restarted from this tree.
Generated Agriculture / Nursery / DUB / 2026-07-01: 106 rows, all 106 with an Actual button, guidance copy present.
Drilled leaf 'Petrol and Diesel Charges': 4 lines, 7 columns, chips read 'Value down' and 'Month down', values 13,500 / 6,500 / 2,000 / 500 summing to the 22,500 footer, equal to the statement cell.

Verified the empty Reference column is real data, not a mapping defect: across the active batch 1,293 of 4,113 rows carry a reference and 3,969 carry a memo, but every row for GL 55010901 has reference null in the source.
Wrapped window.fetch and opened the 'Admin Expenses' aggregate: 0 network calls.
Clicked a leaf inside the panel: body swapped in place, document.querySelectorAll('[role=dialog]').length === 1, seven columns rendered.
Clicked the breadcrumb Back control: returned to the 38-row aggregate list with document.activeElement on the leaf row's Actual.

Checked the table scroll contract: .mis-drill-table-scroll is overflow-x auto, the 701px table scrolls inside the 665px panel, memo text wraps rather than truncating, and the page body never scrolls horizontally.

Applied the emil-design-eng checklist to the new controls: found the pager's :active scale had no transition while every other pressable in the panel eases; fixed to transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) and re-verified.
non_blocking_findings: At a 1024px viewport the 720px panel shows the seven-column table with about 36px of horizontal scroll. It is reachable and the memo wraps, so nothing is lost, but on a narrow window the memo column is the one that pays.
residual_risks: Pagination could not be exercised live: the largest (plant, cost centre, GL) group in the July extract is 18 rows, so no real leaf reaches the server's fixed 100-row page. The pager rendered correctly for the single-page case ('4 matching, rows 1-4 on screen', both controls disabled); multi-page behaviour, the pending policy and the failure-clears-previous-page rule are proven by the vitest leaves against fabricated responses, as the contract requires.
The replaced-pin and stale-pin states were likewise proven against fabricated responses rather than by re-uploading a period mid-session.

automated.summary: All five verify commands pass and all ten required leaves execute under their exact testcase names with non-zero executed counts, read from the junit reports rather than exit codes (vitest exits 0 having asserted nothing when -t matches no leaf, D-0031). Two leaves are deliberately outside the component tests: one drives the api client directly, proving the route, the CSRF header and that pinnedBatches reach the wire untouched - things a mocked client can never prove; and one re-asserts task 2's zero-network aggregate proof as a required leaf of THIS task, so regressing decision 0024 fails here rather than depending on the suite happening to keep it. Design work was done under emil-design-eng and frontend-design; the motion pass found the pager's press feedback had no easing while its neighbours did, and it was fixed.
automated.pass_fail_summary: frontend: 43 tests passed, 0 failed; required leaves: 10/10 executed under their exact testcase name; typecheck, lint, format:check and the production build all clean
remaining_gaps: Pagination, the pending policy, the replaced-pin and stale-pin states are proven against fabricated responses, not client data: the July extract's largest leaf is 18 rows, so no real drill can reach a second page.
